items.text:
This full CMG interview with Elon Musk is a valuable in-depth cross-cultural conversation, covering nearly every cutting-edge field that will reshape humanity’s future, far more than just a regular business talk.

Western public opinion has long imagined China through biased reports and preconceived stereotypes, building a fixed negative narrative. Musk, however, is different. He has visited China many times, traveled to Shanghai and Beijing, ridden China’s high-speed rail, and run Tesla’s Shanghai Gigafactory in depth, gaining plenty of first-hand experience. His remark at the end, “Words cannot adequately describe China”, is no empty polite remark. The amazing productivity of Tesla Shanghai Gigafactory, mature local supply chains, and the strong execution of Chinese engineering teams are conclusions he has witnessed and verified through years of real business cooperation.

The interview touches on a wide range of topics: Tesla Shanghai factory, the launch of Cybercab, iterations of Grok and the explosive pace of AI breakthroughs. He openly talks about the objective gaps between China and the US in AI models and computing power, while emphasizing the need for China and the US to communicate on AI safety. He also discusses China’s massive power generation capacity — electricity is the fundamental foundation behind all AI and robotics industries.

On humanoid robots, he puts forward a striking prediction: 1 billion humanoid robots could emerge within a decade, and in the long run, the global robot population may even reach tens of billions to hundreds of billions, with Optimus as the core product. When massive intelligent robots take over most production labor, the value of wealth and money will undergo fundamental changes. The conversation also extends to Neuralink brain-computer interfaces, education in the AI era, and even the prospect of China-US cooperation in space exploration and Mars missions.

What makes this interview stand out is that Musk breaks away from the black-and-white zero-sum mindset common in Western media. He does not hype up great-power confrontation, nor frame tech competition as a life-or-death contest. Competition exists objectively, yet it does not mean complete isolation. Risks brought by cutting-edge technology are shared by all mankind. AI hazards and space exploration are borderless challenges that no single nation can handle alone.

Most misunderstandings about China among Western audiences stem from consuming second-hand media narratives, without seeing the reality for themselves. Musk’s interview offers an alternative perspective: only by setting aside prejudice, visiting the country, and working with its people can you see the real China. Between major nations, competition can coexist with dialogue. Managing risks and finding room for collaboration is the more rational path for humanity’s long-term future.

AI moves faster than most software development cycles.

A new model can introduce capabilities today that developers could not access yesterday, but the real value emerges when those capabilities can quickly move from a model interface into applications, workflows, and services.

That is where an accessible developer layer becomes important.

With GPT-5.6 available through the AINFT AI Service Platform API, developers have another route for integrating advanced AI capabilities into their own products.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹 𝗜𝘀 𝗢𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁

A capable model sitting on its own does not automatically become a useful application.

Developers need a practical connection between intelligence and software.

That is the role an API can play.

One integration can provide a foundation for intelligent assistants, research systems, automation, coding tools, educational products, customer experiences, and other applications built around AI capabilities.

𝗞𝗲𝗲𝗽𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗨𝗽 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗔 𝗙𝗮𝘀𝘁-𝗠𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗱𝘀𝗰𝗮𝗽𝗲

AI infrastructure cannot remain static while models continue evolving.

Developers need opportunities to incorporate new capabilities without repeatedly reconstructing their entire technology stack.

A platform that expands its available intelligence can give builders more flexibility as their requirements change, potentially reducing the distance between a new model release and practical experimentation.

𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗔𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗧𝗼 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

The larger opportunity for AINFT is not simply making another model available.

It is creating a pathway through which evolving AI capabilities can become components inside products that people actually use.

That is where APIs become important: they turn access to intelligence into something developers can integrate, adapt, and build around.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗜𝗱𝗲𝗮

Every new AI capability is a possibility.

Developers are the ones who turn that possibility into software.

The easier it becomes to connect emerging intelligence with real applications, the faster experimentation can move from the model layer into the products and services built on top of it.

GrokBot is peeking over the edge into Opus 5.

Bots working together or solo deepen knowledge of a given focus. That helps with complex ideas and brainstorming.

Deeper research lets the team gain new skills and perspective, seeing how and why they approach their tasks and pushing past obstacles one solo model cannot.

Grok 4.7 was a letdown in the Grok 4 series, but where that model fails on its own, GrokBot picks up.

Failures of one model upgrade need not hinder the system harness when multiple bots, each with a specialized focus, can make up for the defects of that evolution.

This allows progress to keep moving even if the core model fails to advance on its own.

I have pushed GrokBot to rebrand Vektra and my personal site. I had it study how Fable V and Codex models handle web design from X and online.

After each research cycle, Rin and the team improved like lab researchers, learning what they know and pushing further, combining skills and understanding their limits by making a new agent or informing the teams of issues.

When specialized teams focus on one part of the whole engine, improvements can be made like a surgeon.

I believe GrokBot’s evolution will make individual models secondary for everyday usage, research, and ideas.

Improving GrokBot (which I assume uses Grok 4.7) with Grok 5 under the hood will make it a major powerhouse in software development, AI integration, open-source contributions, and multimedia projects against other models in the field.

It’s almost there—just a little more push in the development of Grok’s core.

@baycYacht @Dennis_Porter_ Not an accurate point of view.  Here's the facts as I understand them instead:

COLDCARD was originally based on a fork of an open-source project.

Later, a competitor of COLDCARD made a second fork, this time using code that had been used (up to that point) in the COLDCARD devices.

THEN, the COLDCARD team got pissed by this open-source competition, because of several things, stating publicly that the competing device was not Bitcoin-only, and that upset them.

As a "solution" COLDCARD abandoned their earlier 100% open source model. In the process, the team added rushed code that was not properly audited.

Yes, technically COLDCARD remained open source after that modification, and technically a security researcher could discover the flawed code.

However -- here is my point -- COLDCARD decided to abandon their earlier 100% open source model, and the rushed choices they made in the switch to a new system directly led to the coding errors.

items.text:
@RonfortMartin Thanks Martin.

The problem I have, as do many others, is the distinction between "agents", when a company makes it appear as if they have no control over a model plus the agentic "swarm" and what happens because the model is somehow too powerful and cannot be controlled/contained and... The company itself taking any kind of responsibility for it's own internal staff, protocols and procedures.

If a company as big as OpenAI, makes the kind of mistakes that allow internet access, when there should be no internet access, that is not a "misaligned model" situation.

It is an incompetence situation.

In a very cramped nutshell, the discourse around the discovered hacking incidents, and any as yet undiscovered, has been focused on the rapid development of powerful models and the potential dangers of these models if they are not contained, controlled and the US government comes up with a closed source preferential regulatory framework that penalises the open source/weight model market.

I agree that the potential threats and dangers are real and should be taken seriously, but I also think that OpenAI have been attempting to shirk their own responsibilities in an effort to avoid consequences by  solely and repeatedly blaming "model misalignment" instead of admitting that their own staff "fucked up big time".

items.text:
I want you to make a 60-second, fully animated explainer video, end to end, completely on your own. I'm stepping away from my computer, so work autonomously until it's done. Don't stop to ask me questions; make the calls yourself and tell me what you decided at the end.

Topic: the journey of photons 

Style: whimsical, charming, storybook. Give the photon a personality. It should feel like a professional motion-design studio made it, not "AI video". The whole thing should be a pure JavaScript animation, rendered from code frame by frame. Don't use AI video generators for the visuals. I've seen the videos people are posting from Opus 5.5 (kinetic typography reels, continuous infinite zooms, data-driven explainers like The Pudding or 3Blue1Brown), and what makes them great is that they're code-rendered: crisp, precise, with a coherent design system and one strong formal idea per scene. Aim for that bar or above.

Make it genuinely educational and accurate. Where you can, simulate the real thing: the random walk should be an actual random walk, not a drawing of one. Include real numbers (core temperature, distance, travel time, years inside the Sun) and be honest about uncertainty in the estimates. Use humor and visual gags to keep attention: onomatopoeia, little characters, callbacks. Put what was happening on Earth during those 100,000 years alongside the photon's timeline.

Deliverable: 1920x1080 at 60fps, exactly 60 seconds, with:
- A voiceover script you write yourself, voiced with the highest-quality text-to-speech model you can access
- Burned-in captions, since most people watch on X with the sound off
- An original music score that fits the whimsical tone and changes with each scene
- Sound design synced exactly to the on-screen action (every bounce, pop, whoosh and ding)
- A professional mix: music ducks under the voice, mastered to streaming loudness

You write the script, design the characters, pick the typography and palette, compose the music, and build the animation engine. Use any tools and resources you can find access to: open fonts, sample libraries, open-source models. Use whatever works.

Quality is paramount. Build verification loops: render stills of every scene and review them critically, check transitions frame by frame, measure the audio mix numerically, fix what's weak and re-render. Don't hand me a first draft. Hand me something you'd put your name on. Also give me the source code so it's reproducible

items.text:
Regarding Anthropic @AnthropicAI , a 2T valuation never made sense to me. Compared to SpaceX @SpaceXAI, Anthropic has no other product lines other than the model itself. Their ARR revenue acceleration was wild but they were the first to produce a model that was useful for coding with a decent lead ahead of others. At this point they are still the leader in coding ability if not by much. Other models can do 95% of the tasks as much less cost and open source models have gotten very good as well. Companies are also turning to open source on prem in order to not give Anthropic their proprietary data. That 2T valuation was justified due to the ARR acceleration would continue but I don’t see that continuing at the same rate. They will still continue to be in the frontier but that is diversifying across multiple models. 

Additionally I believe this is why they are pushing for regulation. Possibly under pressure from their investors.

SpaceX $SPCX has Data centers and ability to stand up compute faster than anyone, Leader in reusable Rockets and capacity by many years, X platform, Starlink which is growing faster than any competitor by far, Solar production ramp, Grok @grok , Cursor @cursor_ai which the team is amazing, and eventually Terafab. All these show real revenue trajectory justifying the valuation.
